summary.short: Framework act promoting AI development and trust in Korea. Covers AI business operators: transparency labelling, safety measures for large-compute AI, and duties for high-impact AI, plus state support and institutions. Enforcement date stated as 22 Jan 2026.
summary.long: The Framework Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and the Creation of a Foundation for Trust (Act No. 20676, dated 21 Jan 2025) sets basic principles and state responsibilities for AI. It establishes a National Artificial Intelligence Committee, an AI Policy Center and an AI Safety Institute, and authorizes state support for AI technology, standards, learning data, startups, clusters and data centers. It applies to AI business operators, including developers and AI-using operators, and to conduct outside the country that affects the domestic market or users. Operators must notify users when using high-impact or generative AI, and label generative outputs and realistic synthetic media. Operators of AI systems above a Presidential Decree compute standard must manage lifecycle risks and report results to the Minister. High-impact AI, defined by listed sectors and rights-affecting decisions, triggers risk management, explanation, user protection and human oversight duties; impact assessment is an endeavour obligation. Foreign operators above Presidential Decree thresholds must designate a domestic agent. Administrative fines of up to 30 million won and imprisonment of up to 3 years for disclosing committee secrets are provided; the Minister may order cessation or correction of violations.

notes: Unofficial English translation by the Korea Legislation Research Institute; its header says it has no legal effect and may not be the latest revision. Enforcement per header: 22 Jan 2026; Addenda Art. 1 says one year after promulgation, with the digital medical device part of Art. 2(4)(d) from 24 Jan 2026. Internal inconsistencies: Art. 7(13) refers to 'The Commission' while the body is the Committee; Art. 8(1)(3) and (4) repeat the same item; Art. 28(1) uses 'Ethical Principles' while Art. 27 defines 'Ethics Principles'; Art. 39(1) has 'Mayer' for 'Mayor'. Art. 41 first paragraph is unnumbered. Art. 43(1) fines cover Art. 31(1) only, while Art. 40(1) investigations also cover Art. 31(2) and (3). Relations list only statutory cross-references; delegations to Presidential Decree and ministerial rules are not recorded here.
